summary: ASTRA is an autonomous astronaut health-monitoring prototype designed for long-duration space missions. It combines personalized health analysis, an interactive 3D digital twin, explainable alerts, NASA research, and offline decision support. Through simulated mission scenarios, ASTRA helps astronauts understand health changes, verify measurements, take informed action, and coordinate with crew medical officers when communication with Earth is delayed or unavailable.
details:
ASTRA — Your Health. Beyond Earth.

The Problem

During long-duration space missions, astronauts face physiological and psychological challenges, including sleep disruption, fatigue, cardiovascular changes, isolation, and delayed communication with Earth. On a Mars mission, medical advice from Earth may take several minutes to arrive, making autonomous health assessment essential.

Our Solution

ASTRA (Autonomous Space Telemedicine & Risk Analytics) is an astronaut health-monitoring prototype designed to support informed decisions when immediate assistance from Earth is unavailable.

ASTRA combines personalized physiological monitoring, explainable alerts, an interactive 3D anatomical digital twin, NASA scientific research, and offline-capable decision support.

Instead of relying exclusively on population averages, ASTRA calculates individual baselines and identifies meaningful changes in available observations. Its Sensor Truth Engine detects questionable, missing, conflicting, or outdated measurements.

Every alert includes an Evidence Passport explaining the underlying readings, the rule that triggered the concern, the reliability of the evidence, and what remains uncertain.

What Makes ASTRA Different?

1. Interactive 3D Digital Twin

Astronauts can explore anatomical systems and understand how available health observations relate to different parts of the body.

2. Explainable Health Monitoring

ASTRA does not simply display warnings. It explains why an alert occurred and identifies the supporting evidence.

3. Autonomous Offline Functionality

Core analysis can continue locally when communication with Earth is unavailable. The mission demonstration illustrates how reports can be retained for later communication.

4. Reliable Data Interpretation

The system distinguishes valid, questionable, missing, simulated, and research-derived information.

5. Crew Medical Coordination

An interactive incident workflow allows astronauts to record follow-up observations, prepare handoffs, and simulate review by a crew medical officer.

6. NASA Research Integration

ASTRA incorporates verified NASA research records from the Open Science Data Repository, human-spaceflight health research, and NASA space-weather information. Research evidence is distinguished from individual physiological measurements.

Technical Implementation

ASTRA uses React Native, Expo Router, TypeScript, React, interactive 3D rendering, browser-based persistence, server-side API integration, and Vercel hosting.

The application combines deterministic monitoring algorithms with scientific evidence and interactive mission scenarios.

Scientific Integrity

ASTRA is an educational research prototype, not a certified medical device.

Its mission scenarios use fictional astronaut measurements, and its alert thresholds are demonstration rules rather than clinically validated diagnostic criteria.

The system explicitly identifies data limitations, missing measurements, and scientific uncertainty.

Challenges and Lessons Learned

Major engineering challenges included maintaining reliable offline functionality, interpreting incomplete or conflicting sensor readings, preserving scientific traceability, integrating NASA research into understandable explanations, and building an interactive demonstration usable across browsers and devices.

Intended Impact

ASTRA demonstrates how transparent, autonomous, evidence-aware software could support astronaut self-assessment and crew coordination during long-duration space missions.

Its broader contribution is a model for understandable decision-support systems that continue to provide useful information when communication with specialists is delayed or unavailable.
